weeks.weekly_summary: Establishing aerobic foundation with easy runs and introduction to tempo work. 5 running days across the week, building from recent Strava activity (16.1 km over 2 sessions). Focus on consistency and conversational-pace development.
weeks.coaching_notes: Athlete shows moderate training frequency (2 runs in last 14 days). Week 1 establishes a sustainable base of 5 runs/week at 7-hour budget. days.notes: Second quality session — unstructured interval work builds mental toughness and aerobic power

weeks.weekly_summary: Volume increases ~9% to 46.5 km. Long run grows to 16 km (+2 km). Two quality sessions maintained (tempo + intervals). Aerobic focus continues with 80% easy distribution. Body adapts to increased weekly commitment.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 2 follows the 8–10% progression rule. Long run grows by 2 km (14 → 16), well within safe limits. Two quality sessions keep intensity stimulus up without overloading. Monitor cumulative fatigue; if RPE on easy runs creeps above 5/10 or HR elevates at given pace, reduce Week 3 slightly and add an extra recovery day.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 3 builds to peak (48 km), with long run reaching 17–18 km. Two quality sessions maintained. This is the hardest week of the block — expect fatigue to be highest mid-week.

weeks.weekly_summary: Peak training week: 48 km, up ~6% from Week 2. Long run grows to 18 km. Two quality sessions (tempo + hill repeats). This is the hardest cumulative week of the block — expect elevated fatigue mid-week. Strong stimulus for aerobic and threshold adaptations.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 3 represents the peak of the block (48 km). Long run reaches 18 km (+2 km from Week 2), testing aerobic capacity. Two quality sessions (tempo on Wednesday, hill repeats on Saturday) maintain intensity. Fatigue will be elevated — monitor HR at easy paces; if resting HR elevates >5 bpm or HRV trends down, Week 4 recovery becomes critical. Keep easy runs truly easy (do not creep into Zone 3). Expect some mental fatigue; stay consistent.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 4 is recovery week: 36 km (−25% from Week 3). Long run drops to 14.5 km (−20%). One quality session only. This is planned recovery to consolidate adaptations and prevent overtraining.

days.notes: First quality session — hills build resilience and quad strength for marathon

days.title: Long Run 18km easy
days.description: Long, easy run at 6:45/km. 2 km longer than Week 2 (16 → 18). Stay disciplined: do not creep faster despite fitness gains. Practice fueling strategy (every 45–50 min). Embrace the time on feet.
days.notes: Peak long run of block. 18 km is a solid distance to build toward marathon prep.

days.description: Recovery day after long run and hill repeats.

days.title: Tempo 8km @ 5:52/km
days.description: Warm up 1.5 km easy (6:45/km), then 8 km steady at tempo pace 5:52/km (lactate threshold, sustainable hard effort). Cool down 1 km easy. Total ~10.5 km.
days.notes: Second quality session — 1 km longer than Week 2 tempo. This is the last hard session before Week 4 recovery.

weeks.weekly_summary: Recovery week: 36 km (−25% from Week 3 peak). Long run reduced to 14.5 km (−20%). One quality session only (tempo). Focus on consolidating adaptations, active recovery, and mental freshness. Set up for next block.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 4 is programmed recovery to allow supercompensation and prevent overtraining. Volume drops significantly (48 → 36 km, −25%), and long run shortens (18 → 14.5 km, −20%), following the recovery-week template. One quality session (tempo on Thursday) maintains some intensity stimulus without stressing the system. Easy runs remain at 6:45/km. Monitor resting HR and HRV — both should improve this week, signaling successful adaptation. Use this week to address any minor niggles, practice fueling, and refresh mentally. Next block will progress from this recovery baseline.
weeks.next_week_preview: After Week 4, the next 4-week block (weeks 5–8) will transition deeper into Aerobic Development, introducing marathon-pace segments within long runs and progressively building long-run distance toward 22–24 km. Without a race date, progression continues on 4-week cycles.

roadmap.weekly_summary: Return to build after Week 4 recovery. Long run grows to 20 km with focus on pacing consistency. Two quality sessions: tempo and fartlek. Introduce marathon-pace awareness.
Long run reaches 22 km. Introduce sustained marathon-pace segments within the long run (final 6–8 km at MP). Build confidence at race pace.
Peak of second block. Long run reaches 23 km with 8 km at marathon pace in middle/final section. Cumulative fatigue will be high — maintain easy effort on recovery runs.
Recovery week 2: −25% volume. Long run back to 18 km. One quality session. Consolidate marathon-pace fitness before next block ramp.

coaching_overview: This 4-week Base Building block establishes a sustainable aerobic foundation for marathon training. The athlete begins with low recent volume (1.15 hrs/week over last 14 days) and progresses to a 7 hrs/week target using polarized training: 80% easy (6:45/km) and 20% hard (tempo 5:52/km, intervals, hills, fartlek). Weekly volume grows 42.5 → 46.5 → 48 → 36 km, following the 10% rule and recovery-week protocol. Long runs progress 14 → 16 → 18 → 14.5 km, building endurance safely. Two quality sessions per week (except recovery week) maintain intensity stimulus: Week 1 (tempo + fartlek), Week 2 (intervals + tempo), Week 3 (hills + tempo), Week 4 (tempo only). No race date is set; the roadmap (weeks 5–8) transitions into Aerobic Development with marathon-pace introduction. Monitor cumulative fatigue, resting HR, and HRV; adjust Week 3 or Week 4 if needed. Athlete should feel fresh and energized by block end, ready for next phase of marathon-specific training.
